theme: Nazareth; the Twelve; John beheaded; the feeding; walking on water
readingInstruction: Read Mark 6:1-56. Jesus is rejected in Nazareth, sends out the Twelve, John the Baptist is beheaded, five thousand are fed, and Jesus walks on the sea. Notice the contrast between those who reject Jesus and those who receive him.
settingTheScene: Jesus returns to his hometown of Nazareth, where he grew up, and meets disbelief. He sends the Twelve out on mission. While they are gone, Mark inserts the story of John’s death, a dark foreshadowing of Jesus’ own. When the Twelve return, Jesus feeds a crowd of five thousand, and that night walks on water. Mark often sandwiches one story within another to draw out meaning.
observation: “A prophet is not without honor, except in his hometown and among his relatives and in his own household” (6:4).
“And he marveled because of their unbelief” (6:6).
“And he called the twelve and began to send them out two by two” (6:7).
“So they went out and proclaimed that people should repent” (6:12).
“When he went ashore he saw a great crowd, and he had compassion on them, because they were like sheep without a shepherd” (6:34).
“And taking the five loaves and the two fish he looked up to heaven and said a blessing and broke the loaves” (6:41).
“Take heart; it is I. Do not be afraid” (6:50).
“For they did not understand about the loaves, but their hearts were hardened” (6:52).
interpretation:
In Nazareth, the people who know Jesus best cannot see who he is. “Is not this the carpenter, the son of Mary?” They take offense at him. Jesus says, “A prophet is not without honor, except in his hometown.” Mark says, “He could do no mighty work there,” except to heal a few. Familiarity and unbelief closed their eyes, and “he marveled because of their unbelief.” Even Jesus was astonished at the hardness of human hearts.

He sends out the Twelve two by two with authority over unclean spirits, with only a staff and sandals. They proclaim repentance, cast out demons, and anoint the sick with oil. The mission of Jesus is multiplied through his disciples.

Mark then tells of Herod’s birthday banquet. Herod had imprisoned John for condemning his marriage to his brother’s wife. Herodias holds a grudge, and when her daughter dances and pleases Herod, he rashly promises her anything. At her mother’s request she asks for John’s head on a platter. Herod is distressed but keeps his oath, and John is beheaded. The faithful prophet dies at the whim of a weak king. It is the shadow of the cross.

When the apostles return, Jesus takes them to a desolate place to rest, but a crowd runs ahead. Seeing them, he has compassion because they are like sheep without a shepherd. He teaches, and when evening comes, the disciples suggest sending them away. Jesus says, “You give them something to eat.” They have five loaves and two fish. He looks up to heaven, blesses and breaks, and gives to the disciples to distribute. All eat and are satisfied, with twelve baskets left. It echoes the LORD feeding Israel in the wilderness and Elisha’s miracle, but it is greater.

That night the disciples are straining at the oars against the wind. Jesus comes to them, walking on the sea. “He meant to pass by them.” This is the language of a theophany, like God passing by Moses. They think he is a ghost. He says, “Take heart; it is I. Do not be afraid,” and the wind ceases. Mark comments that they were astonished, for they had not understood about the loaves, “but their hearts were hardened.” They saw but did not see. Mark is preparing for the question in chapter 8: who is Jesus?
connection: Numbers 27:17 and Ezekiel 34 speak of sheep without a shepherd. Psalm 23 shows the shepherd providing a table. Exodus 16 and 2 Kings 4:42-44 record bread in the wilderness. Job 9:8 says God alone treads on the waves of the sea. Exodus 33:19-23 and 34:6 are God passing by Moses. Isaiah 43:2 and Psalm 77:19 speak of God’s path through the waters. Hebrews 11:36-38 mentions the faithful who suffered.
application:
Is there someone close to you who has trouble seeing Jesus because they know you too well? Pray for them.

Look at the little you have, your five loaves, and offer it to Jesus.

When you are rowing against the wind, listen for “Take heart; it is I.”
prayerPrompts: Confess where your heart has been hard like those who rejected him.
Ask him to teach you to trust him on the water.
